title: 3 Misconceptions Of Effective Classroom Management anagement/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin corrects three persistent misconceptions about effective classroom management: that it must be strict, that the teacher must be stern, and that it takes a long time to establish. He clarifies that what needs to be strict is a teacher's adherence to their own plan, not the severity of the boundaries themselves, which can be set flexibly to match a teacher's preferences. He argues sternness is unnecessary and counterproductive, since simply following through with consequences, calmly and without visible anger, is sufficient, even with a smile. On speed, he contends good management can take hold quickly if a teacher confidently sets highly specific expectations, because the resulting 'shock of excellence' prompts students to rise to meet it. The article closes by insisting teachers should expect impeccable behavior immediately, with total conviction, regardless of a class's prior history.
points: The 'strictness' required in classroom management applies to a teacher's adherence to their own plan, not to how severe the boundaries themselves need to be.
Being stern is unnecessary; consistently following through with consequences calmly, even with a smile, is what actually matters.
Effective classroom management does not require a long runway; confidently set, highly specific expectations can shift behavior quickly.
Setting expectations with unmistakable specificity creates a 'shock of excellence' that prompts students to rise to meet it.
Teachers should expect impeccable behavior immediately and communicate that expectation with unshakable confidence, regardless of a class's past history.
quotes: The only thing that needs to be strict is your adherence to your classroom management plan. As for where you place your boundaries, it’s up to you.
The idea that you have to be hard and severe while managing your classroom endures to this day. The truth is, a stern disposition is a waste of energy.
Good classroom management happens fast if you follow the core principles of SCM . Your confidence in what you’re doing is enough to communicate that your class is different.
When you set your behavior expectations in highly specific detail, whereby students feel the shock of excellence, they sit up straighter. They desire to be better.
You can and should expect impeccable behavior right now . There is no warming up. There is no room for doubt or excuses.
